category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough and consolidation never bridge to neighbouring days. Lesson 1 ends with Tig's exit routine ('A pyramid has 5 faces.') but has no forward hook to Lesson 2's compose/decompose work and no callback line tying these solids to tomorrow's tower-building.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a closing teacher_script line in consolidation that explicitly forward-bridges to Lesson 2 — e.g., Trekker Tig: 'Tomorrow Tig BUILDS a tower from these same solids — we will COMPOSE structures from cubes and prisms!' This satisfies Level 4 cross-referencing.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.rationale names the cylinder/cone trap but cites no research, and recovery_moves = ['Hand-tracing both shapes.', 'Drill point or no point.', 'Compare vertex counts.'] do NOT branch by what the diagnostic told you about the child.
category_feedback.required_fix: Cite a named source (Battista 2007 spatial reasoning OR van Hiele Level 1 visual vs Level 2 analytic) and split recovery_moves into branches: 'If child names solid but mis-counts vertices, drill apex feature; if child cannot distinguish curved from flat, drop back to face-tracing with finger before re-asking name.'

category_feedback.specific_evidence: lesson_specific_materials lists anchor chart, paper Solid Cards (1 set per pair), and sorting hoops. Materials are everyday and puppets are optional, but no explicit NO-PAPER, NO-PURCHASE alternative is offered. for_movement_learners = 'Walk to 5 stations' still requires station setup.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a no-materials path to differentiation: 'No-paper version — children form solid SHAPES with hands/bodies (fists for cubes, palms touching for pyramids) and CALL OUT face/edge/vertex counts. Sorting becomes children moving to corners labelled by attribute count, voice and gesture only.'

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Conceptual progression and precise vocabulary present, but the sort attributes (NAME then FACES then VERTICES) are dictated by teacher prompts — children never INVENT or COMPARE strategies. expanded_walkthrough.rationale does not name the misconception in research-grounded terms (van Hiele or Battista).
category_feedback.required_fix: Insert a 'Geometers Choice' moment in action step 2: 'Pairs INVENT their own sorting rule (by EDGES, curved-vs-flat, tallest-vs-shortest) and explain it; compare two pairs rules.' In expanded_walkthrough.rationale name the principle: 'This is the van Hiele Level 1 to Level 2 shift — from recognizing solids by LOOK to analyzing them by PROPERTIES.'

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Worksheet parts (name 5, count 3 solids, sort 8) directly mirror lesson activities (name 5, count, sort 15) without any TRANSFER task. No part introduces a novel context or item to verify generalization beyond the paper card set children already handled.
category_feedback.required_fix: Convert Part 3 into a transfer task using Canadian context items already in the blueprint: 'Sort these 3 REAL-WORLD objects (Tim Hortons cup, hockey puck, CN Tower top) into the named bin.' Document in worksheet_brief: 'Part 3 introduces 3 unfamiliar real-world items to verify generalization beyond the paper card set.'

summary: Pair 1 is solidly Level 3 across most categories but does not clear the Level-4 bar required for pass. Five categories sit at 3: no forward arc-bridge to Lesson 2; trap is real but uncited and recovery does not branch; no no-paper alternative; sort attributes dictated rather than child-invented; worksheet repeats the lesson format with no transfer task. clarity_voice clears Level 4. Revise both lesson_01 and worksheet_01.
